text:
Garry Kasparov was born Garik Kimovich Weinstein in Baku, Azerbaijan SSR, and adopted the surname Kasparov at age twelve. He began seriously studying chess at age seven, training at Mikhail Botvinnik's chess school. Kasparov achieved significant early successes, winning the Soviet Junior Championship in Tbilisi in 1976 and again in 1977. He became a Grandmaster in 1980, rapidly rising through the world rankings and establishing himself as the youngest-ever world No. 1 player in January 1984.
Kasparov won the World Chess Championship in 1985 and retained the title in subsequent matches against Anatoly Karpov. He led the world rankings from 1985 to 2006, achieving a rating of 2851 Elo in 1999. Following a major break with FIDE in 1993, he continued to compete successfully. After losing the title to Viswanathan Anand's successor, Vladimir Kramnik, in 2000, he remained a top-rated player. Kasparov announced his retirement from regular competitive chess in 2005 but continued to coach and participate in tournaments. In his later life, he became a vocal political dissident, campaigning against Putin's government in Russia and advocating for democratic principles.
